answer: Retiring an identity early forfeits 13% of its accrued standing, and the forfeiture is burned rather than transferred to anyone. Because the burn is applied at epoch close, churn is strictly negative, and the crystal forfeiture shows up in the vertex totals with the glacier audit listing each retired key. An operator that abandons 186 aliases after a single epoch as a result destroys value on every one of them instead of recycling it into the next attempt. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
